name: Soviet Union
sources: No per-nation sourcing note existed when this nation was first entered in init.rs; the table header recorded only "Transcribed-not-invented: approximate 1990 historical starting conditions".
Figures below are transcribed unchanged from that table. Their origin was not documented at the time and is a known gap in provenance.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.9403%/yr. The Soviet Union has no World Bank series of its own, so this is the SUM of all fifteen successor republics' World Bank SP.POP.TOTL (RUS UKR BLR UZB KAZ GEO AZE LTU MDA LVA KGZ TJK ARM TKM EST): 273,146,555 in 1984 to 286,232,551 in 1989, compounded over the five years ending on the eve of the start date. The 1989 sum of 286,232,551 is within 1% of this file's transcribed population_m of 289.0, which is the check that the union has been reassembled and not double-counted.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 11 were held and are listed below with their citations; 37 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): core_packet_internetworking, core_single_mode_fiber, comp_microprocessor, comp_risc_superscalar, comp_relational_database, comm_digital_switching, comm_fibre_optic_backbone, comm_cellular_analogue, ener_seismic_3d_imaging, ener_horizontal_drilling, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, ener_crystalline_silicon_module, matl_semiconductor_lithography, matl_industrial_robotics, matl_lean_production, matl_rare_earth_magnet, matl_stereolithography, aero_stealth_shaping, bio_recombinant_pharma, bio_universal_immunisation, bio_oral_rehydration, bio_cross_sectional_imaging, bio_conjugate_vaccine, bio_monoclonal_antibody, bio_automated_sequencing, tran_container_intermodal, tran_post_panamax_ship, tran_electronic_freight_documents, tran_high_speed_rail, agri_drip_irrigation, agri_composite_membrane, agri_conservation_tillage, agri_integrated_pest_management, agri_protected_cultivation, agri_tissue_culture_propagation, agri_marine_aquaculture, agri_flue_gas_desulphurisation.

COLLISION RESOLVED. Two authoring boards ruled the same cell for this nation and disagreed. The tie-break is uniform across the whole roster and is not a preference between authors: the cell belongs to the board that owns the technology's domain in the registry, which for every non-core id is also its id prefix, and which both cross-domain authors published as their own deferral. matl_composite_structures -> HELD (aerospace-military said not held, materials-manufacturing said held; resolved to the board that owns the Materials domain, materials-manufacturing).

granted.source: Route (a) production, and granted on production evidence which is strictly stronger than the use test this entry carries. CIA, 'The Soviet Microelectronics Industry: Hitting a Technology Barrier', SW 89-10032 (1989), CIA FOIA document DOC_0000498658: the USSR 'achieved full-volume production of first-generation VLSI (1-megabit memories)', albeit with 'device yields well under 50 percent (compared with device yields of 80 percent in US plants)'. The 1-Mbit memory generation is precisely the generation this entry cites. Corroboration for use: an installed base of 500,000-600,000 PCs (Washington Post, 'Perestroika and the PC', 18 June 1990).

Indigenous PAN-based carbon-fibre grades (UKN, Elur, Kulon) were in Soviet production and the material flew: Gravimol carbon-carbon nose cap and wing leading edges on Buran, 15 November 1988, and roughly 5.5 tonnes of composite structure on the An-124, in service from 1986. CoCom makes an imported-fibre explanation for either implausible. WEAKER LEG STATED: I could not pin a named Soviet fibre plant, so the grant rests on the flown artefacts plus the embargo inference and not on a plant citation.

The first Soviet combined-cycle unit (parogazovaya ustanovka, PGU-170) was commissioned at Nevinnomysskaya GRES, Stavropol Krai, in 1972; a larger PGU-250 followed at Moldavskaya GRES in the early 1980s. FLAGGED: this is the least certain grant on my board. The Nevinnomysskaya PGU-170 is a standard citation in Soviet power-engineering histories as the USSR's first industrial combined-cycle installation, but I could not confirm it against a primary source in this session, and the 1990 operating status of the unit is not established here - only that the USSR built and ran combined-cycle plant well before 1990.

The USSR ran a first-rank molecular-genetics base: the Engelhardt Institute of Molecular Biology of the Academy of Sciences in Moscow, founded 1957, and the Shemyakin Institute of Bioorganic Chemistry. The Academy launched a national human genome programme in the late 1980s under Alexander A. Bayev, which is the Soviet counterpart to the American and British programmes of the same years and the institutional evidence that PCR-era molecular genetics was being done at scale. FLAGGED: institutional evidence, not a dated Soviet PCR publication or reagent purchase.

Gorizont, a series of 35 Soviet/Russian geosynchronous communications satellites launched between 1978 and 2000, first flew on 19 December 1978, built by NPO Prikladnoi Mekhaniki (later JSC Information Satellite Systems Reshetnev) on the KAUR-3 three-axis-stabilised bus; the programme was begun to relay coverage of the 1980 Moscow Olympics. Soviet design, Soviet manufacture, Soviet launch.

Gravimol carbon-carbon nose cap and wing leading edges - flight-critical thermal structure - flown on Buran, 15 November 1988, and roughly 5.5 tonnes of composite structure on the An-124, in service from 1986.

VIAM's ZhS-series single-crystal casting alloys, and cooled single-crystal high-pressure blades in the AL-31F, the Su-27's engine, in service from 1985. LEAST CERTAIN OF THE FOUR: I could not pin the year Soviet series production crossed from directionally solidified to single crystal. If that crossing is after 1 January 1990 this cell is wrong and should be withdrawn.

KAB-500L semi-active laser guided bomb, accepted into service 1975; Kh-25ML and Kh-29L laser-guided air-to-surface missiles, the Kh-29 accepted 1980, both used in Afghanistan through the 1980s; 2K25 Krasnopol 152 mm semi-active laser guided artillery projectile, accepted into service 1986. Seeker, control section and the 24N1 designator are all Soviet design and Soviet series production.

NIIP Zaslon (S-800/RP-31) passive electronically scanned array in the MiG-31 — the first phased-array fighter radar to enter service anywhere — with the MiG-31 accepted into service on 6 May 1981; Phazotron N019 Rubin pulse-Doppler in the MiG-29 (in service 1983) and NIIP N001 in the Su-27 (in service 1985); Daryal-type large phased-array early-warning radar operational at Pechora from 1984.

Project 971 Shchuka-B (NATO Akula), lead boat K-284 commissioned 30 December 1984 and in service from 1985 — raft-mounted machinery, anechoic tile and a precision-machined seven-blade propeller; the propeller-milling machinery is the subject of the 1987 Toshiba Machine and Kongsberg export-control case, which is the public evidence that the quieting was real. Project 667BDRM Delta IV SSBN from 1985 to the same standard. The tree's own comment dates the Akula to 1986.

Yantar-4KS1 (Terilen), the first Soviet electro-optical reconnaissance satellite transmitting imagery by radio rather than returning film capsules, first launched as Kosmos-1426 on 28 December 1982, with an operational series flying through the 1980s alongside the film-return Yantar-2K.
